• For SPA style attacks, the best classifiers to use are: Gaussian templates, Support vector machines and Random Forests.

(1) the best classifier to use for error tolerant SPA attacks is Gaussian templates, (2) the best classifier for SPA attacks with s=3 is Support Vector Machines and (3) Random Forests and Support Vector Machines are the best classifiers for error tolerant ASCA attacks.
Gaussian templates, SVMs and Random Forests are the classifiers most likely to be able to return the true value among the first s candidates.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for SPA style attacks, the choice of classifier is not critical and that the most important factor is the number of traces available for training.
SPA style attacks are possible in case of simple leakage and that they are not possible for complex leakage, at least for the configurations that we tested.

, in order to perform SPA attacks with a high probability of success, the adversary should be able to correctly extract the true Hamming weights of the target values with a probability of at least 1/s, where s is the number of Hamming weight candidates that the adversary considers in his attack.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for SPA style attacks, a classifier with high accuracy is not necessarily the one with the highest precision, and vice versa.

, for the first time, we provide a quantitative analysis of the information extraction problem for SPA attacks and we show that the best performing classifiers are not necessarily those used in the literature to date for template-based attacks.
the performance of the classifiers in the context of SPA and ASCA is highly dependent on the leakage model and on the number of ranked outputs that we require the classifier to return correctly.
